walkthroughs.body_html:
Your pancreas keeps blood sugar in a safe range.

Glucose too high: pancreas releases insulin → liver and muscle cells absorb glucose and store it as glycogen.

Glucose too low: pancreas releases glucagon → liver breaks glycogen back into glucose.

Type 1: pancreas can't make insulin (often starts young). Treated with insulin injections and careful diet.

Type 2: body cells stop responding to insulin. Linked to obesity. Treated with diet, exercise, and sometimes drugs.

Both leave blood glucose dangerously high after meals.

Four hormones work as a team across ~28 days:

FSH (pituitary) — matures an egg. Oestrogen (ovaries) — thickens the uterus lining. LH (pituitary) — triggers ovulation around day 14. Progesterone (ovaries) — maintains the lining.
